reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC learned patterns

## Two binary panels separated by a solid-color divider

Observed on task `task-8933d938` (submission verified correct): the input had two equal-height binary panels, separated by a full-width solid divider (color 4 in the test; color 1 in the demo). Return a grid with the panel dimensions, cellwise aligned. The output marks the cells where both panels contain their shared background color, and leaves all other cells as the output background. In the demo, the shared background was color 2 and the marked output color was 3: output 3 exactly where top=2 and bottom=2, else 2. In the test, top background was 0 and bottom background was 0: output 3 exactly where top=0 and bottom=0, else 0. Thus infer panel backgrounds/output palette from the current demo rather than hardcoding colors; equivalently this is the intersection of the two panels' background masks. Output size equals one panel, and the separator is discarded.

Evidence checks from the demo: output row 1 marked columns 4, 7, 9, 10, and 14, precisely the columns where both input panels had color 2. The rule also produced the accepted 10x17 test output.

## Fill gaps in repeated alternating stripes

Observed on task `task-f5e6a59f` (submission verified correct): on a uniform background, rows contain truncated runs of a repeated foreground color with single background-color gaps alternating between them. Fill each single-cell gap between consecutive foreground marks within each run with color 2; preserve all foreground cells and every other cell. The transformation preserves grid dimensions and is rowwise. In the demo, background was 8 and marks were 6; in the test, background was 4 and marks were 8. Inserted color was 2 in both. Importantly, do not fill outside stripe endpoints or larger gaps: for example, isolated stripe pieces separated by a two-or-more-cell break remain unchanged. Identify stripe runs and their single-cell gaps from the current input; do not assume fixed row/column positions. Additional verified instance: the 13x17 test used background 8 and foreground 0, and the accepted output changed each 8 lying between neighboring 0 marks in the same row (i.e. one-cell gaps) to 2; gaps of two or more cells and cells outside the marks remained unchanged. This confirms the operation is strictly rowwise and gap-size selective, even when alternating stripe fragments occur at different columns in different rows.

## Recolor full-length divider lines

Observed on task `task-d6e394f9` (submission verified correct): a grid contains patterned regions separated by complete monochromatic horizontal and vertical lines. Recolor only the full-span divider lines from their separator color to color 2; preserve every other cell, including same-colored fragments that do not form a complete line. In the demo, two full horizontal lines and two full vertical lines of color 1 became color 2. In the test, the full horizontal line of color 6 and full vertical lines of color 6 (including several dividers) became color 2. Detect complete rows/columns in the current grid rather than assuming particular positions or separator colors. A further verified instance of task `task-d6e394f9` had a 19x24 grid with full color-7 divider rows at indices 7, 14, and 16, and full color-7 divider columns at indices 12 and 17 (zero-indexed); recoloring the union of those entire lines to color 2 while preserving every other cell was accepted. Check for intersections only once conceptually; replacing 7 by 2 on the union yields the same result. Another accepted instance was 5x22 with full color-3 divider row at index 4 and full color-3 divider columns at indices 6 and 15; changing the union of those complete lines to color 2 while preserving all other cells was correct. This reinforces that all complete monochromatic rows/columns are recolored regardless of their number or orientation, while partial same-colored marks stay unchanged.

## Stamp a seed shape into zero-cell matches

Observed on task `task-de0375dc` (final submission verified correct): an input contains a small connected seed object in a distinctive color amid a noisy grid, commonly containing 0 and another color. Extract the seed's colored-cell coordinates relative to its bounding-box top-left. Find every in-bounds translation of that exact mask for which all mask positions in the original input are 0; recolor those positions with the seed color. Take the union of all matching placements (overlaps are fine), preserve every other input cell, and keep the original seed. Demos across different seed shapes/colors verified the same-orientation translation rule; do not add rotations/reflections based on guesswork. In this instance, the six-cell color-5 seed's zero-only translated matches produced the accepted output. Validate coordinates and the whole submitted grid carefully; several plausible alternatives (all symmetries, rotations, reflected shape, or matching over the other noise color) were wrong. A second verified instance with the same task id (`task-de0375dc`) used a 9-cell color-2 seed. Relative to its 3x6 bounding box, the mask was `{(0,4),(1,1),(1,2),(1,3),(1,4),(1,5),(2,0),(2,1),(2,4)}`. Exactly five translations over all-zero mask positions were found at top-left coordinates `(1,0),(1,4),(3,9),(4,0),(13,3)`; stamping the union in color 2, preserving all else, was accepted. This independently confirms the same-orientation, zero-only translation rule across different seed sizes/colors and shows that multiple non-overlapping matches can occur.
